answer: An agent’s identity is anchored to a public key generated and kept inside an enclave; a hardware-signed remote-attestation quote binds that key to its MRENCLAVE—the enclave code measurement—and verifies the platform. With key use restricted to the measured enclave, copying a VM cannot reproduce the identity: an attacker must obtain and attest additional genuine silicon, not merely duplicate files. This anchor turns the garden of virtual instances into a costly gale of hardware-backed identities.
